questions.question: Why does every query in the expense service filter by the authenticated user's id?
options: To make queries use the composite index
Prisma requires a userId on every query
To prevent an IDOR bug where a user reads or changes another user's expense just by changing the id in the URL
So that the response can be cached per user
questions.explanation: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) happens when ids are trusted without an ownership check. Scoping by req.user.id, never by a client-supplied userId, closes it.

questions.question: A PATCH handler calls updateExpense.parse(req.body) and the body has amountPaise: -1. With Express 5 and no try/catch, what happens?
options: parse() throws a ZodError, the rejected promise is forwarded to the error handler, which returns 400
The request hangs because the error is not caught
Prisma stores -1 because validation runs after the update
Express returns 422 automatically for any thrown ZodError
questions.explanation: Express 5 forwards the thrown error to error middleware, where the ZodError branch maps it to the standard 400 VALIDATION_FAILED response.

questions.question: What status and body should DELETE /api/v1/expenses/12 return on success?
questions.explanation: 204 No Content signals success with nothing to return; the handler calls res.status(204).end().

questions.question: Why must a GET /expenses/summary route be registered before GET /expenses/:id on the same router?
options: Routes match in registration order, so /:id would capture 'summary' as an id and fail validation
Static routes are slower than parameterised ones
Express 5 forbids static segments after a parameter route
questions.explanation: Express tries routes in the order they were added. If /:id comes first, 'summary' is treated as the id and idParam.parse rejects it with a 400.
